name.description: human-readable label, e.g. 'vLLM prefill TTFT histogram'

engine_id.description: bare engine record id this metric belongs to. One record per (engine, metric): an engine with forty metrics has forty records, each individually correctable and individually citable. Nullable so a generated skeleton validates; an unset value is null, never a placeholder string.

metric_name.description: the metric's name EXACTLY as the engine emits it, including namespace and unit suffix (vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds). The verbatim name is the whole point — it is what a scraper has to match, and a paraphrase makes the record useless for detection work. Nullable so a generated skeleton validates; an unset value is null, never a placeholder string.

metric_type.description: Prometheus-style typing, since that is the vocabulary engines actually document in. log-only = emitted to stdout/a log line and never aggregated; unknown = the engine does not declare a type. Nullable so a generated skeleton validates; an unset value is null, never a placeholder string.

unit.description: seconds, bytes, requests, tokens, 1 (ratio), etc. The unit suffix of metric_name is often but not always the unit; state it explicitly because a mislabelled unit silently breaks every percentile downstream.

exposure.description: how a collector reaches it. http-json and stdout-log are the two that get scraped with a regex and break silently when a version changes the format, which is exactly what a reader needs to know before trusting an absence. Nullable so a generated skeleton validates; an unset value is null, never a placeholder string.

endpoint.description: path or address, e.g. '/metrics' or ':9464/metrics'. Null for in-process APIs with no network surface.

histogram_buckets.description: bucket upper bounds in the metric's own unit, in order. Required for a histogram to be usable: a histogram with unknown buckets gives quantiles that are wrong rather than absent. Null for non-histograms.

labels.description: label keys this metric carries, e.g. ['engine','model_name','finished_reason']. Label cardinality is what decides whether the metric can be used per-model or only fleet-wide.

enabled_by_default.description: true if the metric is on without opting in. false means someone has to turn it on — the single most common reason an 'it does not report X' claim is wrong.

phase_scoped.description: true if the value is attributable to prefill or decode separately rather than to the whole request. This is the distinction that decides whether a metric can explain a TTFT-vs-ITL regression. Nullable in a skeleton for the same reason: null means not established.

verified_negatively.description: true only when the ABSENCE of this metric was actively confirmed against a primary source (the engine's own metrics registry, its docs, or its source tree) at the version named in notes. Without this, 'checked' and 'never checked' are the same record. null = not established.

notes.description: engine version checked, how it was enabled, and any caveat about the value's meaning.

sources.description: source ids; each must exist in data/sources/
